blocks.html:
CLI Reference

This page covers the v0.77.0 binary: 78 top-level commands, 29 of them groups with subcommands, and the global flags at the end, the same commands as v0.76.x. v0.77.0 adds no command. It adds options to eight (soup --version, soup compile-tools, soup export, soup loop init, soup loop watch, soup merge, soup registry push and soup ship), gives soup train --cloud a third provider, and removes AWQ and GPTQ export; those changes are collected under v0.77.0: new, changed and removed flags. Since v0.77.0 upstream also generates a complete reference of every command, option, type and default from the code, docs/cli-reference.md at v0.77.0: use it as the exhaustive list. This page is the curated index, with the behaviour notes and exit codes the generated page does not carry. The generated page renders the --help strings as they are, so its soup mcp serve --allow-mutating and --allow-execute entries carry the stale help text that says execution never happens (see MCP server). Six commands are new in v0.76.0 (soup rewind, soup bench train, soup data clean, soup recipes verify, soup adapters check and soup adapters audit), and soup bench became a group whose infer subcommand is the old inference benchmark; they and every other v0.76.0 change are collected under v0.76.0: new commands and flags, and Every top-level command is an index with the page that documents each one.

Exit codes are defined per command, not uniformly across Soup. Since v0.76.0 eleven gate and verdict commands share one taxonomy: 0 pass, 2 gate failure, regression or drift, 3 usage or input error, and a mistyped flag on one of them is 3 as well. Every other command keeps its own scheme (a few individual codes moved too, see what moved), and a mistyped flag on those is still 2. A CI step that tests for exit 1 as "the gate failed" now lets a failing gate through (what moved). Exit codes lists what each command returns.

Core Commands

soup init

Create a config file with interactive wizard or template.

blocks.code: soup init [--template <template>] [--output <path>]

blocks.html:
soup train

Start a training run.

blocks.code:
soup train [--config <path>] [--resume auto|<checkpoint>] [--wandb] [--tensorboard] \
           [--deepspeed zero2|zero3|zero2_offload|zero3_offload|zero++|zero_pp] [--fsdp full_shard|shard_grad|full_offload] \
           [--gpus auto|<N>] [--nodes <N> --node-rank <R> --master-addr <host> [--master-port <port>]] \
           [--no-reexec] [--gate <suite>] \
           [--push-as <user/repo>] [--hf-resume] [--yes]

blocks.html:
• --gpus (v0.27) — GPUs per node for distributed training (auto or an integer): Soup detects NVLink vs PCIe and re-launches under accelerate launch. Since v0.76.0 it exits with the launcher's exit code on every platform; on Windows it now waits for the launcher (through v0.75.2 the call returned 0 at once). --no-reexec prints the launch command instead of launching it and exits 1 (it does not exit 1 when --dry-run is also given).
  • --nodes, --node-rank, --master-addr, --master-port (v0.76.0) — multi-node Accelerate launch. --nodes above 1 requires --gpus (GPUs per node, the same on every node) and --master-addr; --master-port defaults to 29500. A launch-setting mistake exits 1 with Invalid distributed launch: .... See multi-node launch.
  • --deepspeed zero++ (v0.27) — ZeRO-3 with quantized weights & grads
  • --gate (v0.26) — run an eval suite at epoch boundaries and halt on regression
  • --push-as (v0.29) — auto-push every save_steps checkpoint to HF Hub as a checkpoint-<N> branch
  • --hf-resume (v0.29) — pull the latest checkpoint branch from HF Hub and resume training
  • --cloud modal|lambda|runpod with --gpu <type> and --cloud-submit — plan-only unless you add --cloud-submit; see serverless cloud training. Each provider has its own --gpu list; for RunPod it is a100 (the default), h100, a40, rtx3090 and rtx4090. --cloud runpod is new in v0.77.0 (it was refused through v0.76.x): plan-only by default it writes a stub and contacts nothing, and --cloud-submit needs RUNPOD_API_KEY and RUNPOD_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY (a path to the private key, with its .pub beside it) and otherwise exits 1. It has not been run against a real RunPod account yet (tracked as #2098). Upstream states that it makes one attempt, copies the results back once with a 15-minute limit into a new directory next to the output path, deletes the Pod afterwards, and does not upload local input files, so the base and the data must be reachable from the Pod; see RunPod. Any other --cloud value exits 2 with Invalid --cloud.
  • --yes (-y) skips the Start training? confirmation. Since v0.77.0 a run whose standard input is a pipe or a redirected file exits 3 without it (stdin is not a TTY, so the start-training confirmation cannot be answered. Pass --yes to start without the confirmation.), and piping y into the prompt no longer answers it, so pass --yes in scripts and CI jobs. --dry-run does not ask.

soup chat

Interactive chat with a trained model.

blocks.code: soup chat --model <path> [--base <model>] [--temperature <float>] [--max-tokens <int>]

blocks.html:
soup serve

Start an OpenAI-compatible inference server.

blocks.code: soup serve --model <path> [--backend transformers|vllm|sglang|mii] [--port <int>] [--host <host>] [--tensor-parallel <n>] [--gpu-memory <float>] [--speculative-decoding <draft-model>] [--num-speculative-tokens <n>] [--adapters <name>=<path>]

blocks.html:
--adapters (several named LoRA adapters on one server) works with --backend transformers only; with vllm, sglang or mii it exits 1. To serve one adapter on vLLM or SGLang, pass the adapter directory itself as --model: the base model is read from its adapter_config.json (on SGLang the adapter is applied since v0.77.0; through v0.76.1 every answer came from the base model, see Serving).

--auto-quant exits 2 with --auto-quant is unavailable since v0.76.0: Soup cannot measure quantization candidates before an engine has loaded them, so it refuses instead of guessing a format. Any --host other than loopback needs --tool-auth-token, which gates the tool, thumbs and adapter routes only; the generation routes take no token on any backend. Since v0.77.0 POST /v1/tools/python and POST /v1/tools/bash need the token on every bind, loopback included, and answer 401 without it; the token can also come from SOUP_TOOL_AUTH_TOKEN. Both routes answer 501 without running anything unless the host provides OS-level isolation (transformers backend only). The isolation cuts the network; the code still runs as the server's user, and /v1/tools/python, where it runs, still runs inside the RLVR code sandbox's timeout and memory limit. See Serving.

soup export

Export model to deployment format.

blocks.code:
soup export --model <path> --format gguf|gguf-ud|onnx|tensorrt|bitnet|tq1_0|torchao [--quant <type>] [--output <path>]
soup export --model <path> --format gguf [--verbose] [--no-install-deps] [--llama-cpp <dir>]   # v0.77.0: --verbose and --no-install-deps are gguf only
# awq and gptq were removed in v0.77.0: --format awq|gptq exits 1 and names the formats that remain,
# and --bits, --group-size and --calibration-samples were removed with them (exit 2, No such option).
# --calibration-data is now for --format gguf-ud only. Stay on v0.76.x if you still need AWQ or GPTQ export.
soup export --format onnx [--onnx-task text-generation|feature-extraction]              # feature-extraction for task: embedding
soup export --model <path> --format gguf --deploy ollama [--deploy-name <name>]          # export, then deploy; the Ollama name defaults to soup-<model-name>

blocks.html:
--deploy is validated before anything runs (v0.76.0): it accepts only ollama, and only with --format gguf, gguf-ud, bitnet or tq1_0. Any other combination exits 1 (--deploy is not supported for format 'onnx'. Supported formats for deploy: gguf, gguf-ud, bitnet, tq1_0).

soup merge

Merge LoRA adapter with base model.

blocks.code: soup merge --adapter <path> [--base <model>] [--output <path>] [--dtype float16|bfloat16|float32] [--save-format fp16|4bit|4bit_forced] [--low-memory]

blocks.html:
--low-memory (v0.77.0) merges tensor by tensor straight from the base model's safetensors files instead of loading the whole model into RAM. It needs the default --save-format fp16 and a plain LoRA adapter: DoRA, modules_to_save, rank or alpha patterns and adapters on the embeddings are refused. Upstream states that the values are identical to the regular merge. With a Hub base it is one of the paths that consult the namespace pin (Supply chain security). See Model export.

soup push

Upload model to HuggingFace Hub.

blocks.code:
soup push --model <path> --repo <user/repo> [--hub hf|modelscope|modelers]
  [--private] [--collection <owner/slug-hash>] [--message <commit message>]

blocks.html:
• --collection (v0.29) — add the pushed repo to an existing HF Collection

Token resolution for --hub hf: env HF_TOKEN / HUGGINGFACE_HUB_TOKEN > ~/.cache/huggingface/token > ~/.huggingface/token. The legacy --token flag is deprecated and delegates to this chain.

Each other hub authenticates with its own credential, and that is new in v0.75.1. --hub modelscope reads MODELSCOPE_API_TOKEN, --hub modelers reads MODELERS_TOKEN, and neither reads HF_TOKEN any more. Before it, the chain above ran for every hub and the resolved Hugging Face token was handed to the third-party SDK, so pushing to ModelScope or Modelers disclosed a token that is often write-scoped (0.53.10 to 0.75.0). Rotate it if that was you.

soup eval

Comprehensive model evaluation platform.

blocks.code:
soup eval benchmark --model <path> [--benchmarks <list>] [--fewshot N] [--batch-size N] [--run-id <id>] [--device cuda|mps|cpu] [--trust-remote-code]
soup eval custom --model <path> --tasks <path> [--trust-remote-code]
soup eval judge --target <pairs.jsonl> [--model <judge-model>] [--provider openai|server|ollama] [--rubric <path>] [--api-base <url>] [--run-id <id>]
soup eval auto [--config <path>]
soup eval compare <run1> <run2>
soup eval leaderboard [--sort-by <benchmark>] [--format table|json|csv]
soup eval human --input <prompts.jsonl> --model-a <path> --model-b <path> [--output <results.json>]
soup eval gate --suite <suite.yaml> [--model <path>] [--baseline <registry://id|scores.json>] [--regression-threshold 0.05] [--write-baseline <file>]
soup eval citation <data.jsonl> [--style bracket|inline|footnote] [--shuffle-seed <n>] [--output <scores.json>]
soup eval against <baseline-run-id> --candidate <run-id> [--metric task_accuracy|refusal_rate|format_validity|p95_latency_ms|custom|aider_polyglot|judge:<model>|benchmark:<lm-eval-task>] [--suite <locked.json>] [--json-only]
soup eval quant-check --before <model|registry://id> --after <model|registry://id> --tasks <tasks.jsonl> [--format table|json|markdown] [--allow-stub]

blocks.html:
Notes on the rows that have more to them than the form shows:

  • soup eval benchmark wraps lm-evaluation-harness, so it needs pip install "soup-cli[eval]". --benchmarks is a comma-separated list (default mmlu), --fewshot falls back to each benchmark's own default when you leave it out, --batch-size defaults to 8, --run-id links the results to an existing training run, and --model may be a LoRA adapter directory.
  • soup eval leaderboard reads the experiments database and exits 1 with No eval results found. until soup eval benchmark or soup eval custom has recorded something. --sort-by applies to the table only: --format json and --format csv print the whole leaderboard without sorting by it. A --format value other than json or csv is not rejected; you get the table.
  • soup eval human is interactive, so it needs a terminal. It generates both models' answers to each prompt (a JSONL file whose rows have a prompt field), shows them side by side and asks a, b, tie or q. q ends the session early and the judgments so far are still scored and saved. The result is an Elo table, written with the judgments to --output (default human_eval_results.json). Both model paths must exist locally.
  • soup eval gate exits 0 when the suite passes, 2 when a task fails or regresses against --baseline, and 3 for a setup you can fix: a suite that is missing, outside the working directory or fails its schema (since v0.76.1 also one over 1 MiB, nested deeper than 100 levels or expanding past its alias allowance), a --baseline that cannot be resolved, a --regression-threshold outside 0.0 to 1.0, --write-baseline without --model, or an unknown flag, and since v0.77.0 a suite with no tasks or a repeated task name and a baseline score that is not a finite number. It exits 1 when --model cannot be loaded or on an unexpected exception, such as a suite that is not valid YAML. Through v0.75.2 a failed gate and a broken invocation were both 1, so a CI job could not tell them apart by the exit code. Everything else about it, including --write-baseline, is on the eval gate page.
  • soup eval against compares two recorded runs with a paired bootstrap and exits 0 for no regression, 2 for a regression, and 3 for a bad flag, a missing or invalid --suite, or no recorded metric series for either run. The pre-push hook from soup eval gate-install calls it.
  • soup eval quant-check exits 0 on OK or MINOR, 2 on MAJOR, 3 on a usage or input error such as an unknown --format, a path outside the working directory or a .gguf path, and 1 when a model fails to load, which since v0.76.0 stops the command. --allow-stub scores with deterministic stub generators instead; the output then carries a stub marker ("stub": true in the JSON) and an OK means nothing was measured. A --tasks file that is not valid JSONL exits 1. See quant-check.

On soup eval judge, --target is a JSONL file of prompt and response pairs you already generated (every line needs a prompt and a response field; soup infer writes exactly that shape), not a model, and --model names the judge. --api-base is the judge's endpoint: plain http is accepted only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1, and since v0.75.2 an IP literal that is private, link-local or reserved is refused on https as well, with loopback still allowed. A hostname is not resolved, so the check narrows what a URL can name directly; it does not make an internal host unreachable by name. See what v0.75.2 refuses.

soup deploy

Deploy models to inference runtimes.

blocks.code:
# Ollama
soup deploy ollama --model <gguf> --name <name> [--system <prompt>] [--template <tpl>] [--parameter <key=val>] [--yes]
soup deploy ollama --list                # only models whose name starts with soup-
soup deploy ollama --remove <name>       # any Ollama model, by name

# HuggingFace Spaces (new in v0.29)
soup deploy hf-space \
  --model <user/repo> \
  --space <user/space> \
  --template gradio-chat|streamlit-chat

blocks.html:
soup deploy hf-space validates model_repo via validate_repo_id before substituting into app.py / README.md — a crafted repo id cannot inject Python code into the deployed Space. Instead of --template it accepts --template-dir <dir> (custom app.py + README.md, optional requirements.txt, {MODEL_REPO} placeholder; details on Hugging Face Hub integration), plus --private and --yes.

soup infer

Batch inference on a list of prompts. With --task asr (v0.71.32) it transcribes a JSONL of audio clips through a Whisper model or adapter and reports per-row and corpus WER/CER when reference texts are present. See ASR fine-tuning.

blocks.code:
soup infer --model <path> --input <path> --output <path> [--max-tokens <int>] [--temperature <float>] [--batch-size <n>] [--cuda-graphs]
soup infer --task asr --model <whisper|adapter> --input <jsonl> --output <jsonl> \
  [--audio-dir <dir>] [--asr-language <lang>] [--asr-task transcribe|translate]

blocks.html:
soup migrate

Import config from competing tools.

blocks.code: soup migrate --from llamafactory|axolotl|unsloth <input-file> [--output <path>] [--dry-run]

blocks.html:
soup recipes

Browse and use ready-made training configs.

blocks.code:
soup recipes list                          # List all 171 recipes
soup recipes show <name>                   # Print recipe YAML
soup recipes use <name> [--output <path>]  # Copy to soup.yaml
soup recipes search <query>                # Search by model/task/size
soup recipes verify [--config <soup.yaml>] [--json] [--templates|--no-templates]   # v0.76.0: can the LoRA adapter attach? checked on the meta device, no weights downloaded

blocks.html:
soup recipes verify is one of the eleven commands on the 0 / 2 / 3 taxonomy: 0 when everything that could be checked attaches, 2 when a config cannot attach, 3 for a missing or unparseable --config or a usage error, 1 for a crash. A gated repository or a base that needs trust_remote_code is reported as unverified and does not change the exit code, so an exit 0 can mean nothing was checked. It needs the [train] extra (torch, transformers, peft); without it the command exits 1, after it has checked --config (since v0.77.0 a missing, unparseable or refused --config exits 3 first, on any install). soup recipes use exits 3 for a recipe the catalog marks unavailable (kimi-k2-sft and kimi-k2-thinking-grpo at v0.77.0) and writes nothing. See Recipes.

Data Commands

blocks.code:
soup data inspect <path> [--rows <n>] [--image-dir <dir>]  # View dataset stats (--rows: sample rows to show, default 5; --image-dir is new in v0.76.0)
soup data validate <path> [--format <fmt>] [--min-valid-fraction <0.0-1.0>]  # Check format compliance; exit 3 input error, 2 no usable rows or below the fraction
soup data clean <path> [-o <out>] [-f] [--dry-run] [--min-tokens <n>] [--prune-echo] [--strip-boilerplate] \
  [--repair-code] [--repair-json] [--drop-invalid-json] [--json]   # v0.76.0: sanitise a dataset, never modifies the input
soup data convert <path> --to <fmt> --output <f>  # Convert between formats
soup data merge <f1> <f2> --output <f> [--shuffle]  # Combine datasets
soup data dedup <path> [--threshold <float>]      # Remove duplicates
soup data stats <path>                            # Extended statistics
soup data generate --prompt "..." --count <n>     # Generate synthetic data
soup data generate --provider openai|local|server|ollama|anthropic|vllm  # Multi-provider support (openai is the default)
soup data generate --template code|conversation|qa|preference|reasoning  # Domain templates
soup data generate --quality-pipeline             # Validate + filter + dedup
soup data generate ... --batch-size <n>           # Examples per API call (default 5)
soup data filter <path> [--coherence <f>] [--perplexity <n>] [--ppl-model <id>] [--field <name>] [--score-only]  # Quality filter; perplexity is scored with gpt2 unless --ppl-model says otherwise
soup data sample <path> --strategy random|diverse|hard -n <n> [--pct <0-100>] [--seed <n>]  # Sample subset
soup data split <path> --val 10 --test 10 [--absolute] [--seed <n>]   # Split; --val/--test are integer percentages
soup data split <path> --val 10 --stratify <field>           # Stratify on a field
soup data split <path> --val 10 --stratify-semantic --num-clusters <n>  # TF-IDF + K-Means strata (v0.73.2, needs scikit-learn); not combinable with --stratify
soup data search <query> [--limit <n>] [--sort downloads|likes|lastModified|trending|createdAt]  # Search HuggingFace Hub
soup data preview <dataset_id>                               # Preview remote dataset
soup data download <dataset_id> [--output <path>] [--samples <n>] [--split <split>] [--format alpaca|sharegpt|chatml] [--hub hf|modelscope|modelers]  # Download (default split: train)
soup data register <name> --path <path> --format <fmt>       # Register local dataset
soup data unregister <name>                                  # Remove from registry
soup data registry                                           # List registered datasets
soup data push --input <jsonl> --hf-dataset <user/repo> [--private] [--message <text>] [--hub hf|modelscope|modelers]  # Publish JSONL as a dataset repo (v0.29)
soup data mix --optimize --datasets <a.jsonl,b.jsonl> [--budget 1h] [--num-probes <n>] [--seed <n>] [-o mix_recipe.yaml] [--overwrite]  # Mixture search; WITHOUT --live the proxy is synthetic
soup data mix --optimize --live --base-yaml <soup.yaml> --datasets ...   # --live REQUIRES --base-yaml (real short training runs)
soup data mix --apply <mix_recipe.yaml>                      # Prints the data: block to paste into soup.yaml; writes no dataset
soup data from-traces --logs <logs> --format langchain|openai|soup-serve  # Trace-to-preference (v0.26); for soup-serve --logs is the directory `soup serve --trace-log` writes, and a single file is refused
soup data review <pairs.jsonl>                                # Preview preference pairs (v0.26)
soup data augment --input <jsonl> --strategy rephrase|translate|style     # LLM augment (v0.25)

blocks.html: Experiment Commands

blocks.code:
soup runs                         # List all training runs
soup runs show <run_id> [--no-plot]   # Detailed run info + loss curve (--no-plot skips the curve)
soup runs replay <run_id> [--no-plot] # Re-render a finished run's summary and loss curve from its stored metrics
soup runs curriculum-curve <run_id> [--history <curriculum_history.jsonl>] [--width <4-200>]  # Dynamic-curriculum bucket weights (BETA)
soup runs compare <run1> <run2>   # Side-by-side comparison
soup runs delete <run_id>         # Remove from database
soup runs clean [<run_id> | --all] [--dry-run] [--force] [--keep-weights/--no-keep-weights]
                                  # Reclaim checkpoint space: by default drops optimizer and scheduler
                                  # states only; --no-keep-weights deletes whole non-best checkpoints (the one with the
                                  # lowest loss recorded at its step is kept whole; with no recorded loss, the latest)

blocks.html:
soup doctor --disk is opt-in because the probe costs roughly 9 seconds cold and 2.4 seconds warm on Windows, and with several physical disks it reports the worst one. Since v0.73.3, on Linux, it may also write a 64 MiB scratch file named .soup-diskprobe-* into the directory it is probing (the current directory for soup doctor --disk; a training run probes the shard directory instead), read it back with O_DIRECT to time a sequential read, and delete it, because on a disk whose rotational flag cannot be trusted the media type is settled by a measured read rather than by the flag. On Windows it only runs the disk query. It exists because the streaming disk tier requires NVMe and refuses a SATA SSD, a spinning disk or media it cannot identify, rather than guessing and thrashing for hours.

soup quantize quantizes nothing: it prints the soup export command to run. For --to gguf that command carries --quant q4_K_M (and q8_K_M for --bits 8), which soup export refuses, because its --quant is case-sensitive and accepts only q4_0, q4_k_m, q5_k_m, q8_0, f16 and f32: retype it in lower case, and use q8_0 for 8 bits. --to takes gguf, onnx or tensorrt; since v0.77.0 --to awq and --to gptq exit 2 (--to must be one of ['gguf', 'onnx', 'tensorrt']). Through v0.76.x they printed a --bits form with a Deprecated: line.

soup monitor reads nvidia-smi on NVIDIA systems. On Apple Silicon it reads /usr/bin/powermetrics through sudo -n, which never prompts for a password, so run sudo -v first or the command exits 1 and tells you to.

# The [aider] extra is NOT enough to run it: you also need the official Aider
# benchmark image, source-built from an Aider checkout (./benchmark/docker_build.sh),
# and a clone of polyglot-benchmark. --allow-host-services lets untrusted
# model-generated code reach other services listening on the host.
soup train --config soup.yaml --cloud lambda   # plan-only by default, like --cloud modal
# soup export --format gptq needed --calibration-data from v0.74.0 until the format was removed in v0.77.0
soup serve --model ./output --host 0.0.0.0 --tool-auth-token "$TOKEN"     # exit 2 without the token
soup sweep --config soup.yaml --param lora_rank=8,16   # not a config key (the rank is lora_r): exits 1
                                                       # before the first arm, instead of running a grid

blocks.html:
Two scope notes on those lines. --tool-auth-token is the bearer token for the tool, /v1/thumbs and /v1/adapters routes of the transformers backend (since v0.77.0 the Python and Bash tool routes need it on every bind, loopback included); generation, /v1/models, /health and /metrics carry no token on any backend, so a non-loopback bind publishes the model to whoever can reach the port, and an authenticating reverse proxy belongs in front of it. The vLLM, SGLang and MII backends do not read the token at all. Serving has the route-by-route table. And --param takes a shortcut name (lora_r, lr, epochs, batch_size and so on) or the full path (training.lora.r); a bare lora.r is not either: since v0.77.0 --dry-run refuses it before printing a grid ('lora' found at both root and training level, exit 1), and a sweep in which every arm fails exits 1 (one completed arm still exits 0). Through v0.76.1 every arm of such a sweep failed when its config was built, while the command still exited 0 with failed rows.

Limits worth knowing before you script them, each stated as upstream behaves at v0.76.0:

  • soup rewind --json writes no file when the run had no spike (it prints No loss spikes recorded. and exits 0), and writes NaN or Infinity, which is not strict JSON, for a non-finite loss.
  • soup adapters check needs NumPy although it does not need PyTorch (through v0.76.1 it also needed the safetensors package and exited 1 on a bfloat16 weights file; since v0.77.0 it reads the file itself and widens bf16), exits 1 on an MLX adapter (the MLX trainer names its file adapters.safetensors), and reports inactive for a non-LoRA PEFT adapter such as VeRA. Its scope is LoRA adapters saved by the transformers path.
  • soup recipes verify exits 0 when everything it could check attaches, which can mean everything was unverified (a gated repository, or a base that needs trust_remote_code).
  • soup data clean ignores --strip-boilerplate and --prune-echo on dpo and kto rows without saying so.
